exercises.instruction: Put pairs of opposite words into the table.
items: right / wrong (Example row printed in table)

exercises.instruction: Fill the gaps with an adverb (e.g. wrongly) so that the second sentence means the same as the first.
items: Example: The numbers in this list are wrong.
This list is .......... wrongly .......... numbered.
1 He was driving at 140 kilometres per hour.
2 He shouted her name.
3 We went past the baby’s bedroom, making very little noise because she was asleep.
We went past the room very ......................... .
4 He’s a good pianist.
He plays the piano really ......................... .
5 There was ice on the road, so we drove at 20 kilometres per hour.
6 She was very unfriendly when she spoke to us.
7 I don’t swim for the school team because I’m a bad swimmer.
8 The manager was quick to reply to my letter.
The manger replied to my letter ......................... .
9 She looked at me in a very sad way.
10 Our teacher is always friendly when she corrects our mistakes.

exercises.instruction: Answer the questions, using adverb forms of the words in the box. Write full sentences.
items: 1 I can’t hear what the child is saying.
How is the child speaking?
2 Glen was acting in a way that no one could understand.
How was Glen acting?
3 The accident happened in one short moment, and no one was expecting it.
How did the accident happen?
4 Pippa passed the exam with no problems at all.
How did she pass the exam?
5 He finished the job in less than a minute.
How did he finish the job?
